text.p: Rayonier Inc chairman and chief executive Ronald Gross said all of the company's businesses are "fairly stable".
He said the company continues to benefit from its cost reduction programs and that "barring any unexpected market changes, second quarter results likely will be similar to the first quarter."

Rayonier issued the statement as it reported first quarter 1997 earnings of $18.4 million or 62 cents per share on sales of $260 million. First quarter 1996 earnings were $31.5 million or $1.05 per share, on sales of $294 million.

Rayonier is a global supplier of specialty pulps, timber and wood products. The company has 1.5 million acres of timber in the U.S. and New Zealand. About 55 percent of Rayonier's sales are to international customers in 70 countries.
